name: Meridian Coffee Roasters

do: Talk about the farmers and the roast, not just the flavour notes
State the origin, the roast, and the shipping window as plain facts
Say what an offering does not include as plainly as what it does
Use everyday words a customer would use out loud
dont: Use wine-tasting jargon: no 'notes of', no 'terroir', no 'mouthfeel', no 'palate'
Never claim a health benefit of any kind
Never call the coffee artisanal, curated, craft, or hand-crafted
Never call anything revolutionary, world-class, or the best
Do not describe the roastery as a journey, a ritual, or an experience
Do not mock the reader's current coffee or the people who sell it

offerings.name: Roaster's Choice Subscription
offerings.description: A rotating 340g bag of our current favourite single-origin, roasted fresh and delivered every four weeks.

offerings.name: Origins Gift Box
offerings.description: A one-time gift box with three 200g bags from three different origins, plus a tasting card.

positioning: For people who check the roast date before the price, Meridian roasts to order in small batches and ships within 48 hours of roasting, so the bag that lands is weeks fresher than anything that has been sitting on a supermarket shelf.

composition_plan.intent: First screen is the first row of the split, not a banner: the narrow column labels the business and where it roasts, the wide column states the freshness promise and gives one way to act on it. Off-centre, no full-width band.
The conviction behind the operation set large, with the narrow column holding the sourcing detail that backs it. This is where the flip happens: the label column moves to the other side of the rule.
The sequence from green bean to delivery, one line per step, so the freshness claim reads as a procedure rather than a boast. Ordered list supplies the numbering.
The catalogue side by side, one column per offering, each column carrying both what is included and what is excluded, so the exclusions sit at equal weight with the inclusions.
The given figures — weights, intervals, timings, the founding year — each under a short label, presented as the spec row that closes the argument on freshness.
The practical logistics a first-time buyer stalls on: shipping, skipping, cancelling, what is out of scope. Answers open in place, in the narrow-label rhythm of the rest of the page.
Street address, phone and email as a plain ruled block, establishing that this is a real neighbourhood roastery with a door, and nothing else.
